industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying a view that moved inside the industry this week: Software B2B Enterprise goes to Neutral on the rotation into software, Semiconductors stays Underweight on the AI capital spending re-pricing, Hardware stays Neutral with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): the market has stopped paying for AI capital spending (hyperscaler prints gave no lift, ABB sold on data-centre orders) while demand is intact and sub-sector upgrades continue (memory, equipment, power electronics), and the software-against-semiconductors factor pair is reversing (Goldman Sachs' desk, 26 October). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: B now, B prior. The industry row stays C because the industry is split by the rotation itself. Counter-case for D: the Nasdaq down 6% in two weeks with momentum down 15% is a regime statement about this industry; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Neutral, carried, inside a split industry, with the evidence moved against it at the margin. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Danske Bank TMT (27 October) says hardware is giving back gains as software works again, though some falls are overdone for names whose demand is mostly outside AI (HMS Networks, 80% outside AI), and the optical and power demand read of last week stands. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, D prior. One live holding, Hexatronic (4.95%, Technical Momentum B, Fitness 60.3), judged in component 4. Balanced; Neutral by judgement. To D if relative strength falls to F with the rotation into software continuing; to B if the optical demand read is repeated with the shares.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
